summary: Corning bills itself as the "Olive Capital of the World," and that's not hollow boosterism — the Sacramento Valley floor surrounding this 3.5-square-mile town is dotted with some of California's oldest and largest olive orchards, and a major olive oil processing facility operates here, anchoring an agricultural economy that also leans heavily on walnuts, almonds, and cattle. At a median home price of $274,600 against a median household income of $55,732, the price-to-income ratio lands around 4.9 — strikingly affordable by California standards, though a $1,116 median rent still claims roughly 24% of that same median income, so the math is tight rather than comfortable. The landscape is dead-flat valley floor, hemmed by the Coast Range to the west and the Cascade foothills to the east, which means summer highs push well into the 90s and 100s while winters stay mild and foggy — the 9.1 hours of daily sunshine reflect a climate that's genuinely blazing from June through September. Interstate 5 bisects the town, creating a fragmented feel between the east and west sides, and most employment beyond agriculture and food processing requires a roughly 25-mile commute south to Red Bluff or farther to Chico. Corning is, at its core, a small agricultural service town that happens to sit in one of California's last affordable corridors — with the tradeoff being that affordability tracks directly with remoteness.
